settings.name_in_paper: adversarial multi-armed bandit (bandit online decision problem) against adaptive adversary
settings.definition_quote: Assume that $c_1,c_2,\ldots\in [0,1]^n$ is a sequence of cost vectors. There are $n\geq 1$ experts. ... Then an adaptive adversary is a function $A:[0,1]^{n\times t-1}\times \{1\ldots n\}^{t-1}\to[0,1]^n$.

settings.name_in_paper: bandit with countably infinitely many arms/experts with prior weights, adaptive adversary
unmapped: countably infinite arm set; each arm has a prior weight w^i known to the learner, weights summing to at most 1; regret bound depends on the reference arm's weight
settings.definition_quote: The adversary subsequently generates cost vectors $c_t\in[0,1]^\infty$, and at each time $t$ we have to select one index or expert $i$ and incur its cost $c_t^i$. We learn only the cost of the selected expert. As a prerequisite, we need that each of the infinitely many experts is associated with a prior weight $w^i$

algorithms.name: FPL using all observations with oracle sampling probabilities
FPL using all observations with Monte Carlo estimated sampling probabilities
bFPL for infinite expert class (entering times)

source.label: thMain
source.quote: Let $\gamma_t=\min\big\{1,t^{-\frac{1}{3}}\big(n\sqrt{\log n}\big)^{\frac{2}{3}}\big\}$ and $\eta_t=\frac{\gamma_t}{n^2} t^{-\frac{1}{3}}\big(n\sqrt{\log n}\big)^{\frac{2}{3}}$. Then, for any $T\geq(n\log n)^2$, each expert $i\in\{1\ldots n\}$, and \emph{any} adaptive assignment of the costs $c_1,c_2,\ldots$, bFPL satisfies the regret bound $\Expect c\leqT\bfpl-c\leqT^i \leq 4\Big(Tn\sqrt{\log n}\Big)^{\frac{2}{3}}$.

results.notes: n = number of experts = K. Regret is E[cost] minus cost of fixed expert i, for each i (max outside expectation), so recorded as pseudo-regret. Parenthetical: for T<(n log n)^2 regret at most (n log n)^2. Also holds for label-efficient setting per Section 4.

conditions: sampling probabilities P(I_t = i) are provided by an oracle

source.label: thChati
source.quote: The algorithm FPL (\ref{eqFPL}), obtaining cost estimates according to (\ref{eq:chati}) and with learning rate $\eta_t=\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{2nt}}$ achieves a regret of at most $\Expect c\leqT\fpl-c\leqT^i \leq 2\sqrt{2Tn\log n}$ for any $i\in\{1\ldots n\}$.

results.notes: Requires oracle access to FPL's sampling probabilities (computationally infeasible per paper). Adaptive adversary.

tuning: k = ceil(2 t^2 log(2 sqrt t)) Monte Carlo samples per round

source.quote: Let $\gamma_t=\frac{1}{2\sqrt t}$ be the exploration threshold. ... by sampling the perturbed leader $k=\big\lceil2t^{2}\log(2\sqrt{t})\big\rceil$ times ... Then the algorithm FPL (\ref{eqFPL}) with learning rate $\eta_t=\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{2nt}}$ achieves a regret of at most $\Expect c\leqT\fpl-c\leqT^i \leq 2\sqrt{2Tn\log n} +7\sqrt T$ for any $i\in\{1\ldots n\}$.

results.notes: O(t^2 log t) samples per step; polynomial time per round.

symbols.w_i: prior weight of the reference expert i (weights sum to at most 1)

conditions: prior weights w^i sum to at most 1

source.label: thInf
source.quote: Consider a bandit problem with countably many arms/experts, each expert $i$ having a prior weight $w^i$ such that the weights sum up to at most $1$. Then the above described bFPL variant with entering times $\tau^i=\left\lceil\big(\frac{1}{w^i}\big)^8\right\rceil$, exploration rate $\gamma_t=t^{-\frac{1}{4}}$, and learning rate $\eta_t=t^{-\frac{3}{4}}$, satisfies the regret bound $\Expect c\leqT\bfpl-c\leqT^i \leq O\left(\Big(\tfrac{1}{w^i}\Big)^{11}+T^{\frac{3}{4}}\log w^i\right)$ for all $T\geq 1$

results.notes: Recorded as written; 'log w^i' is presumably meant as log(1/w^i) (as written it is negative). Formal proof omitted in paper.
